players.product: Regulated electric service to data-center customers under electric service agreements (ESAs) with minimum take provisions

quarterly_data.quarter: Duke Energy press release: Duke Energy protects customers from data center costs (10-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: North Carolina large-load (data center) settlement: Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Progress reached an agreement with the North Carolina Public Staff; other parties include Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Carolina Industrial Group for Fair Utility Rates and the U.S. Department of Defense. Terms: a nonrefundable, upfront payment for grid facilities serving only that customer (such as a substation); upfront deposits and security guarantees for grid upgrades that serve all customers (such as transmission lines); and new large-load customers, including new data centers, must take service under a separate High Load Factor rate schedule. If approved by state regulators it would apply to all large-load customers (50 megawatts or more with 80% load factor) that sign an ESA in North Carolina after June 1, 2026; Duke previously required large loads of 100 megawatts or more to agree to protective contract terms, and ESAs signed before June 1 contain similar protections. It adds to the Customer Protection Plus framework announced in July. A North Carolina Utilities Commission decision is expected by mid-November. North Carolina president Kendal Bowman: 'data centers will pay upfront for all costs to connect to the grid.'
quarterly_data.figure: large load = 50 megawatts or more with 80% load factor (previously 100 megawatts or more); ESAs signed after June 1, 2026; NCUC decision expected by mid-November
